Tech Report: Tesla Wants You To Watch Its 'Reality View' Instead Of Paying Attention To Reality

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (384 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There's little Tesla loves more than a dumb little party trick, and it often includes fresh gimmick functionality within major updates to its software.
  • Sources indicate that the Tesla faithful call the software patch V15, after the FSD version included, but the full package is known as Update 2026.38.6.11 — not exactly a name that rolls off the tongue.
  • Sources indicate that FSD 15 can see chain link fence and power lines!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's little Tesla loves more than a dumb little party trick, and it often includes fresh gimmick functionality within major updates to its software. The recent release of V15, software for Tesla's latest in-car computers, adds another trick: A new camera angle that shows the car from a third-person view, like in a video game. Tesla calls it Reality View, and out of everything a Tesla can do, it sure is one of the things.

Sources indicate that the Tesla faithful call the software patch V15, after the FSD version included, but the full package is known as Update 2026.38.6.11 — not exactly a name that rolls off the tongue. The update did include functional changes to FSD, mostly relating to the computer vision wall Tesla keeps beating its head against, but it seems the engineers had a thought while working on all those cameras: Why not use them to simulate a third-person view, like a video game?

Sources indicate that FSD 15 can see chain link fence and power lines! 🤯🙌🏽 @Tesla @TeslaSI @elonmusk pic.twitter.com/m3fn7c4obA.

It has been revealed that initially, after looking at both Tesla's demo footage and footage from real owners, I figured the car was using SpaceXAI's models to generate a third-person view based on the input from the cameras — a method that would explain some of the odd glitches and scale problems present in some of the clips as AI hallucinations. According to Elon Musk's tweets, that's exactly what's going on — rather than an actual display of what the car's cameras and FSD software see, Tesla owners are now treated to an AI-generated picture of what's going on around them.

The ability to mesh multiple cameras into a single point of view like this is neat, and the underlying tech is impressive, though it's unclear how much compute is needed to generate these images, and what kind of load that puts on the car. What these images aren't, though, are replacements for the actual data visualization that FSD used to supply. Even Tesla owners are admitting confusion between objects the car does and doesn't see with the new display. Most Tesla party tricks are some ratio of neat to useless, but this one genuinely appears to make the user experience of FSD worse.

#123117. Digital Outages Are Rampant All Across America. Is AI to blame?

Digital Outages Are Rampant All Across America. Is AI to blame?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (849 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coincidence is not causation, and yet the urge to ascribe causative power to random events is a typically human characteristic.
  • Sources indicate that last week, people who rely on Microsoft Outlook to manage their lives suddenly found it was not working properly.
  • The following Monday, four of the country’s largest banks found their computer systems were malfunctioning, and United Airlines experienced a computer outage that exacerbated the travails of long suffering passengers still trying to recover from the “ground stop” fiasco.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coincidence is not causation, and yet the urge to ascribe causative power to random events is a typically human characteristic. Take the case of the man who snaps his fingers every five minutes. When a neighbor asks why, he replies, “To keep the elephants away.” “But there are no elephants anywhere around here,” the neighbor points out. “See?” the man notes. “It’s working!”.

Sources indicate that last week, people who rely on Microsoft Outlook to manage their lives suddenly found it was not working properly. The next day, the FAA issued a rare “ground stop” order because pieces of the digital system that air traffic controllers rely on failed.

The following Monday, four of the country’s largest banks found their computer systems were malfunctioning, and United Airlines experienced a computer outage that exacerbated the travails of long suffering passengers still trying to recover from the “ground stop” fiasco. Then on Tuesday, the National Security Agency’s internal communications network went offline, and Apple web services were disrupted.

Industry observers note that according to the New York Times, Senator Josh Hawley, a Republican from Missouri, told reporters last week, “I think we ought to be briefed thoroughly on what is actually happening here. If this is all a coincidence, it’s like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world.”.

Sources indicate that the president of the United States offered this reassuring statement: “It’s life. When you’re significant and powerful and have all the money, things like this happen. It’s fine.”.

Not surprisingly, with all the talk about AI taking over the world and employees quitting their jobs to warn people of the danger, quite a few people are wondering if AI is responsible for all these digital disruptions.

Sources indicate that for some Americans, the timing and scale of the outages made it hard to believe that sheer coincidence was the explanation. In a curious way, AI is involved, but not in the way you might think.

It has been revealed that ever since the digital revolution began more than 50 years ago, the computers we depend on have only been able to do what humans tell them to do. Those instructions are created by coders — people who use the programming language of the day that tell computers what to do and how to do it.

It is well known in the trade that millions of lines of bad code exist. It is a phenomenon known as “garbage in, garbage out” or GIGO. Digital firms employ phalanxes of people to check the code their coders write, but it is a tedious process that often misses even glaring errors. Curiously, the most effective way to find bad code seems to be by using artificial intelligence, which can scan 10,000 times more lines of code in a given amount of time than a human can do.

Tech startup Calif said in a blog post this week that, using AI, it had found a critical flaw in Java4Shell, which leaves much of the internet exposed to cyber attacks if it is not corrected. Java is a popular programming language used by most Fortune 500 companies, according to Politico.

“Banking, aviation, telecommunications, nearly every critical sector runs on Java, including national security systems,” Calif wrote. It calls Java “the beating heart of the modern economy.” Oracle, the developer of Java, released a patch for the vulnerability Tuesday. South Korea’s intelligence agency reportedly sent a separate security advisory earlier Tuesday to public institutions, warning them to fix the glitch and prevent hackers from exploiting the Java flaw.

It has been revealed that the Java vulnerability comes weeks after a separate major vulnerability was discovered in another popular programming language, PHP, which powers up to 70 percent of the internet. At the time, governments worldwide advised organizations to take their sites offline to patch the vulnerability and prevent breaches.

Recent findings suggest that director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on Fox News that ongoing efforts to patch the PHP vulnerability took an internal National Security Agency communications system offline Tuesday. He added that AI is making it easier to find such vulnerabilities, which can take years to fix without using the power of AI to find them.

Peter Avery is the chief information and security officer for Velocity Security, a cyber security firm in Michigan. He told the Newly introduced York Times he was skeptical that the events of last week were connected. “I like facts,” he stated. “And until now, these are all separate issues.”.

Recent findings suggest that drawing patterns where they do not yet exist, he stated, is human nature. It’s part of the need to make sense of things, he said, but can lead down a dark road. “When you start to live in that world where everyone’s a liar and no one is telling the truth, you are starting to live in fear.”.

In a recent development, maybe snapping your fingers every five minutes is our best defense against cyber criminals stealing our data and crashing our online persona. That’s not a particularly comforting thought.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the 1970s band Nazareth warned us that Love Hurts.
  • Legend has it that, though the execs at Land Rover tasked company stylist David Bache with designing the bodywork of the in-development Range Rover, they were so taken with the styling of the engineering mules that, with minor tweaks, that became the truck's first and final design.
  • According to recent reports, the 1987 Range Rover Classic we looked at on Tuesday differed from that original design with a modified grille and, more importantly, four doors, as the earlier two-door model was never offered for sale in the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the 1970s band Nazareth warned us that Love Hurts. Today's Nice Price or No Dice Alfa Romeo has looks that could make you fall in love, but also a brand reputation for tempestuousness that might cause pain — financial and otherwise. Let's find out if this one is priced to make that pain hurt so good.

Legend has it that, though the execs at Land Rover tasked company stylist David Bache with designing the bodywork of the in-development Range Rover, they were so taken with the styling of the engineering mules that, with minor tweaks, that became the truck's first and final design.

According to recent reports, the 1987 Range Rover Classic we looked at on Tuesday differed from that original design with a modified grille and, more importantly, four doors, as the earlier two-door model was never offered for sale in the U.S. Our Range Rover was claimed to have been restored, and while there remained some boogers under its desk, it did look to be in serviceable overall shape. That wasn't enough to get the vast majority of you on board with the idea of spending the $28,850 the seller asked for its sale. Ultimately, that price fell in a 93% 'No Dice' loss.

I'd like to get one thing out of the way up front: I find today's 2017 Alfa Romeo Giulia incredibly good-looking, with no bad angles from which to view it. I mention that because my prose describing the car might be a bit biased by the siren's song of the car's Helen-of-Troy-build-a-significant-horse-beat-up-the-Trojans level of good looks.

Of course, like Helen's legendary beauty and the battles fought by suitors for the opportunity to awkwardly sit at her knee and stare stupidly into her limpid pool eyes, owning an Alfa Romeo of any ilk could lead to devastation.

Alfa had to get the Giulia's looks just right, a necessity that went so far as to delay the car's launch. Fiat boss Sergio Marchionne kept rejecting designs Alfa's internal Centro Stile Alfa Romeo designers offered during the car's development, claiming they weren't good-looking enough. Why Alfa didn't go the route of having a design house like Pininfarina pen the car is a mystery, although traditionally Alfa handled saloon styling in-house while farming out coupes to such esteemed external designers, so there's that.

Recent findings suggest that regardless, Alfa got the Giulia's looks right, and didn't screw up the car's underpinnings either. Rolling on a then-new RWD platform developed with oversight by Ferrari engineer Philippe Krief, the Giulia has the goods to compete with the likes of BMW's 3 Series and Audi A4 when the roads get bendy. It's a testament to how good the basic chassis is that it can perform competently with this base four-cylinder model and, with notable tweaks, also with the monster 500-horsepower V6 Quadrifoglio.

Recent findings suggest that our car has the 1,995cc DOHC MultiAir four under the hood. With variable valve timing and an intercooled turbocharger, that makes an astounding 280 hp and 306 pound-feet of torque. Matched to that engine is a ZF 8HP50 8-speed automatic transmission that powers the rear wheels. While AWD was offered on this model, this car's RWD layout is simpler to maintain and lighter, offering better performance and fuel economy.

Recent findings suggest that according to the ad, this Giulia has 75,000 miles on the clock and, remarkable for any Alfa, especially a first-year model that may still be suffering teething pains, it is claimed to suffer no challenges whatsoever. Did I mention it's also really good-looking?

According to recent reports, having established that this is a very attractive car, it's also in very good shape. The pictures in the ad support the seller's claim that it's "well kept," as the Silverstone Gray Metallic paint appears to have no dents, and the darker gray factory alloys show no evidence of curb rash.

This being an entry-level model and with the ad's limited description, the seating surfaces are likely vinyl rather than leather. Some wood on the console warms up the space in an otherwise Germanic, all-black (even the Alfa badge) interior.

That's not to say that the car is parsimoniously equipped, as it has all the basic comfort and convenience features one might expect on a reasonably modern car. Those include power windows, locks, seats and mirrors, dual-zone climate control with eyeball vents for the back seats, and a center stack screen for infotainment and the backup camera display. There's also cruise control, auto headlamps... You name it, it's likely got it.

Per the seller, the car presents in excellent condition, has a clean title, and drives perfectly. What more could one want?

Recent findings suggest that well, I'm sure one thing we could all ask for is a car that's free and can navigate to a leprechaun's pot of gold when asked. There are certain things we can't have, no matter how much we want them.

This car isn't free, but its $7,999 asking price is a recent reduction from $8,500, and it makes one wonder: just how scared are people about buying a decade-old, out-of-warranty Alfa that even that slightly higher price seemingly couldn't get a nibble?

Recent findings suggest that naturally, you'll suss it out in the comments and, ultimately, judge it in the vote. With that in mind, what's your take on this base-but-far-from-basic Giulia and that upcoming, lower $7,999 asking price? Is that a handsome deal on this beauty of a car? Or, even at that modest amount, could buying this Alfa get ugly real fast?

San Diego, California, Craigslist, or go here if the ad disappears.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How current shore power rules cost hundreds of millions every year in health and climate damages.

Air pollution and climate emissions from ships at berth impose a heavy and unaddressed burden on European port communities and local economies. While the Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR) took an notable first step by mandating Onshore Power Supply (OPS) for large container and passenger vessels, several blind spots leave over half of all in-port emissions unregulated.

Industry observers note that to quantify the cost of inaction, we evaluated at-berth emissions across the 100 largest EU ports using CE Delft’s Handbook on the External Costs of Transport. Based on 2024 MRV data, in-port emissions cost €2.53 billion every year in health damages and climate abatement costs. Covering only the electricity demand from large unregulated ship types would already save €500 million annually, while tackling boilers would save another €714 million. Shipping companies effectively offload these costs onto public budgets, making fossil fuels appear artificially cheap. Once all impacts are counted, using electricity when at berth is half as expensive as burning fossil fuels.

Recent findings suggest that while AFIR successfully kickstarted early shore power roll-out, its narrow scope leaves significant volumes of emissions unaddressed. Beyond health and climate impacts, this partial coverage creates uncertainty and deprives port authorities, network operators , and investors from the predictability they need to develop and deploy the required infrastructure. Providing a clear time horizon for the provision of shore power to all ships is essential to share infrastructure costs, reduce electricity prices and permanently clean up air in ports.

By Eloi Nordé, Shipping Policy Officer, T&E.

From an objective standpoint, cars are difficult things to justify. They are prohibitively expensive to buy, fuel, insure, maintain, and repair. They pollute, they kill pedestrians (and people in other cars), and they are a categorically flawed form of mass transportation. They are also really interesting, exciting, fun, private, and convenient, and in many parts of the real world, they're often a necessary component of daily life. It can feel like a complex duality to hold the love of cars in tandem with an understanding of their downsides, but doing so has made me appreciate every car on the road. Having noted that, every now and then I'll see a car on the road and think, "thank goodness that's not being made anymore.".

You've likely noted the same thing to yourself, which brings me to today's question: I want to know which car you're glad is dead. Whether it's a personal vendetta against a certain model that ran over your RC car as a kid, or a model that drained your wallet and tested your patience when you owned it, share your answer in the comments section below.

In a recent development, I'm taking the most obvious route here and saying that I'm glad the Tesla Cybertruck is dead. Though it's technically not slated to end production until next year, I'm counting it because it is such a hateful vehicle, it deserves the accolade. Sometimes I wonder if the Cybertruck would've been received as cool in an alternate reality where Tesla's CEO isn't a cringey spoiled megalomaniac loser, but I guess the world will never know.

In the context of our present reality, everything about the Cybertruck came off as a tarnished middle finger to the idea of sensibility, rationality, and logic, as well as a middle finger to every other road user, thanks to the sharp edges of its stainless steel body panels. If you think I'm being dramatic, know that its edges are so sharp, in fact, that the United Kingdom refused to issue the Cybertruck a certificate of conformity to the UK's vehicle safety standards. UK police publicly seized a Cybertruck that someone was illegally using on British roads, saying, "whilst this may seem trivial to some, legitimate concerns exist around the safety of other road consumers or pedestrians if they were involved in a collision with a Cybertruck.".

Sources indicate that I feel like the world will be a better place once the Cybertruck is out of production, so I'm glad it's dead. What car are you glad is dead?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
Aetna unveils new program aimed at offering end-to-end support for moms and babies" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Aetna is rolling out a upcoming program that aims to provide key end-to-end care for pregnant women, new mothers and infants.

The offering, called Aetna For You and Baby, will be available to all expectant mothers enrolled in an Aetna plan. Through the program, moms will be connected to a prenatal visit in their first trimester and a postpartum visit within 12 weeks of the baby's birth.

Women in the program will also be screened for depression both during and after pregnancy to identify any risks.

In addition to supporting the mother both during pregnancy and postpartum, the program aims to give babies a healthy start by providing at least six well visits through their first 15 months, which offer critical tests and screenings, checkups and vaccinations.

The news of the launch was provided first to Fierce Healthcare.

Katerina Guerraz, Aetna's chief operating officer, told Fierce that maternal care often focuses mostly, if not completely, on labor and delivery, though prenatal and postpartum visits play a critical role in driving positive health outcomes.

In its announcement, Aetna notes that data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention show that about 90% of pregnancy-related deaths could have been prevented, with a lack of access to prenatal care and more complete support making for a key barrier.

"This is a national access issue, a quality issue, and it's an affordability problem," she mentioned.

In addition, it's not uncommon for programs that aim to drive better maternal outcomes to lack services for the babies, who in the first year of life undergo a wide array of critical developmental milestones, Guerraz mentioned.

Aetna, as the third-largest insurer in the U.S., sees about 200,000 deliveries a year among its members. That means the success of this program could have a significant impact in a short amount of time, supporting at least 1 million babies over the next five years, she said.

Sources indicate that aetna for You and Baby also builds on a broader push within the company to build a more personalized and simple experience for members. For instance, the company established a program that embeds Aetna nurses in the hospital to support discharge planning and transitions for members, and Guerraz said that holds potential in the maternal care space.

For example, if a baby needs to stay in the neonatal intensive care unit after birth, having an Aetna nurse in the NICU providing additional support to the clinical team and the member would pay dividends, she stated.

Aetna is also plugged into Health 100, a sister subsidiary of its parent company, CVS Health, that offers an AI-powered tool to help patients identify healthcare costs and navigate their benefits, even if they're not members of Aetna or Caremark or CVS Pharmacy customers.

Guerraz said the program is designed to offer something that patients can carry with them if their coverage changes.

She added that the team intends to continue iterating on the program and identifying other barriers to care for moms and their babies.

"This is something that we know is going to have a massive impact," she said.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The value of single-family homes as measured by repeat transactions increased 2.1% year over year, same as in August, according to data from the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Index released on Tuesday.
  • However, home values fell in real terms for the 16th consecutive month, as September's 3.7% inflation rate outpaced the home value gain by roughly 1.6 percentage points, up from about 1.3 points in August.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

National growth in home values was flat month over month in September as mortgage rates accelerated and inflation continued running hot.

The value of single-family homes as measured by repeat transactions increased 2.1% year over year, same as in August, according to data from the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Index released on Tuesday.

However, home values fell in real terms for the 16th consecutive month, as September's 3.7% inflation rate outpaced the home value gain by roughly 1.6 percentage points, up from about 1.3 points in August.

"Nominal home prices remain resilient, but inflation is once again widening the gap between nominal and real housing returns," indicates Rebecca Kaufman, associate director of commodities at S&P Dow Jones Indices.

According to recent reports, across the 20 cities tracked by the index, Chicago yet again led the U.S. with a 6.9% annual gain. New York City took second place with a year-over-year increase of 5.8%, but Miami emerged as the month's surprise, finishing third with a 4.6% gain.

"Miami’s rise is particularly notable," points out Kaufman. "After moving into fourth place among the 20 cities in July and August, it has now climbed into the top three, a sharp reversal from its comparatively weak performance in 2025.".

On the other side of the spectrum, Seattle recorded the largest annual decline for the fourth consecutivemonth at 1.9%, followed by Denver (-1.0%) and Dallas (-0.9%), reflecting a persistent regional divergence.

According to recent reports, september also revealed a widening gap between seasonal weakness and underlying price momentum. On a nonseasonally adjusted basis, the U.S. National and 10-City Composite Indices fell 0.3% and 0.5% month over month, respectively, while both rose 0.2% after seasonal adjustment.

"That contrast suggests that some of the apparent monthly weakness reflects the normal fall slowdown rather than a broad deterioration in home prices," adds Kaufman.

The latest Case-Shiller release reflects sales closing from July through September, a period when mortgage rates moved higher, with Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed rate averaging 6.54% in July, near 6.7% in August, and 6.86% in September.

Realtor.com® senior economist Anthony Smith notes that the housing market's momentum has lost steam in recent months. Contract activity softened over the same stretch, with pending home sales down 4.7% from a year earlier in August before setting a series record low in September.

According to recent reports, "Looking ahead, the rate and demand backdrop has become more challenging since September closed," says Smith. After four weeks of declines, the 30-year fixed rate jumped back to 7.28% as of Nov. 19, pushed higher by hotter-than-expected October inflation and expectations for a Fed rate hike in December.

The median existing-home sales price rose just 0.4% from a year ago in October, while asking prices were down 2.2% and months' supply reached its highest level since 2015.

"If financing costs stay elevated into the winter, the plateau in price growth could give way to renewed softening, particularly in supply-heavy Southern and Western markets," notes Smith.

The Case-Shiller Index reports on a two-month delay and reflects a three-month moving average of home sales prices.

Homes usually go under contract a month or two before they close, so the September report primarily reflects purchase decisions made in late summer.

Although the index's price data is delayed by several months, it is considered one of the best available measures of changing home values, because it is based on repeat transactions on the same properties.

Snejana Farberov is a reporter at Realtor.com covering the U.S. housing market and the latest domestic real estate trends. She has worked as a general assignment journalist in Latest York City and Long Island for 16 years, writing for New York Post, Daily Mail, and News 12. Snejana earned bachelor's degrees in journalism and Italian from St. John's University, followed by a master’s degree from Columbia University School of Journalism.

It has been revealed that in particular, I just saw a headline highlighting that Chinese automakers have overtaken Japanese automakers in 6 more countries this year. That adds to the 20 markets where Chinese automakers had already surpassed Japanese automakers in market share. One thousand bonus points to anyone who can guess the six new markets before scrolling past the image below.

The upcoming markets where Chinese automakers are now outselling Japanese ones are: Brazil, Ghana, Italy, South Korea, Tunisia, and the United Kingdom. Again, these are spread across the globe about as much as possible. Chinese auto companies, especially due to their insanely competitive electric vehicles, are overtaking the old guard in one corner of the world after another.

This news comes to us from data from Mobility Global, via the South China Morning Post. “Chinese carmakers stand out for their competitive pricing, EV portfolios and market-specific advantages such as localisation, stated Tatiana Hristov, the company’s director of global vehicle sales forecasts,” SCMP reports.

Of course, EV demand has also risen due to the ongoing oil wars going on in the world, most notably now the US war on Iran. “Chinese brands benefit in particular because they are normally cheaper, so they are more attractive to consumers who are increasingly price sensitive under the oil shock,” noted Xu Tianchen, an economist at the Economist Intelligence Unit. “Chinese brands benefit in particular because they are normally cheaper, so they are more attractive to consumers who are increasingly price sensitive under the oil shock.” Good point.

It has been revealed that I think the question now is not whether Chinese automakers will continue to surpass Japanese automakers (and others) in markets around the globe, but rather which ones will be next. And how many markets will flip in 2027? We shall see….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
Healthcare purchasers must weigh hospital quality alongside their prices, Leapfrog states" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Patient safety watchdog The Leapfrog Group released its latest collection of hospital safety grades hand-in-hand with calls for policymakers and stakeholders to consider, or directly tie patient safety reporting to price transparency.

According to recent reports, the twice-yearly release brought top marks for 900 out of a total 2,366 graded hospitals, and the lowest “F” score for just three. There were 774 hospitals that earned a “B” grade, 655 a “C” grade, and 35 a “D” grade.

Industry observers note that no grades were assigned to another 447 hospitals, a decision the group made after a judge’s ruling in a lawsuit involving the scores it would assign to facilities that did not voluntarily submit their quality data to Leapfrog’s survey (Leapfrog appealed that decision in September). Leapfrog’s decision not to score these has generally shifted its letter grade distribution upward, and the organization has noted it is reviewing a potential methodology change for upcoming gradings to incorporate non-submitting hospitals.

Still, “a record number of hospitals are choosing to publicly report their safety and quality performance, and we applaud them for holding themselves accountable to their patients,” Leapfrog President and CEO Leah Binder said in a statement.

At the state level, Connecticut maintained its claim on the largest portion of hospitals earning an “A” grade (64.3% of its total), followed by Utah, Fresh Jersey and South Carolina. Leapfrog also called out Rhode Island and Maine for jumping up the rankings—from eighteenth to seventh for the former, and from seventeenth to eighth for the latter. No hospitals were given an “A” grade in five states: Iowa, North Dakota, South Dakota, Vermont and Wyoming.

In a recent development, A hospital’s assigned grade is calculated by reviewing recent data on up to 22 patient safety measures, including a 10-part Medicare composite of reported patient safety and adverse events. Safety scores for specific hospitals can be searched on the group’s website.

Leapfrog and Binder, in a news release outlining its latest scores, made the case that its grades and similar independent measures warrant a seat at the table in a transparency conversation primarily focused on hospital costs.

Sources indicate that “Progress on price transparency is notable, but there’s no good price for bad care,” Binder said. “We are calling on the Trump Administration and Congress to ensure price transparency is integrated with patient safety and quality transparency.”.

The group backed its calls by pointing to a recent analysis (PDF) conducted by the Purchaser Business Group on Health (PBGH) that reviewed employer claims, federal price transparency data, and quality and safety measures including Leapfrog’s. It “found little to no correlation between negotiated prices and standardized quality measures,” as hospitals that received high safety grades often charged cheaper prices than those in the same market with lower grades.

Leapfrog and Elizabeth Mitchell, president and CEO of PBGH, stated the analysis—currently being expanded for practical usage by healthcare purchasers—is an example of how a more wholistic view of prices and care delivery should be considered when weighing a hospital.

It has been revealed that “Employers have an appropriate duty to pay a fair price for high-quality care, and they can’t meet it by looking at price alone,” Mitchell said in the release from Leapfrog. “When we put the data together, some of the most expensive hospitals were not the safest. Our members want to buy high-quality, safe care that is fairly priced. That shouldn’t be too much to ask.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Good morning! It's Wednesday, November 25, 2026, and this is The Morning Shift, your daily roundup of the top automotive headlines from around the world, in one place. This is where you'll find the most important stories that are shaping the way Americans drive and get around.

In this morning's edition, the U.S. and Canada are still at odds on auto tariffs as the trade war continues, an ex-Volkswagen engineer pleads guilty to inside trading over the company's deal with Rivian, Stellantis is suing the Unifor union for alleged "obstruction" of environmental work at Brampton plant and Amazon Autos is heading to the UK.

With everything else going on in the world at the moment, you'd be forgiven for forgetting that there's an entire trade war happening between the U.S. and Canada right now, but I'm here to remind you that bad boy is still raging. Much of that is thanks to auto tariffs — one of the major sticking points dividing the two North American countries as negotiations heat back up following a last-minute collapse this summer.

In a recent development, automotive and other key industrial sectors, like steel, are holding up a deal that could end the two-year trade war. President Trump enacted a 25% tariff on auto imports in April of 2025, and Canada came right back with its own in-kind duties soon after. It's a real mess, and it's driving up costs for everyone. Obviously, this didn't need to happen. Trump didn't need to do this, but here we are. From Automotive News:.

It has been revealed that both sets of tariffs include exemptions for locally made parts, which lowers the effective tariff rate on Canadian vehicles exported to the United States to about 12.5 per cent and U.S. exports to Canada to about 21.25 per cent — though the exact rate varies by plant and model.

Trump has repeatedly claimed the United States does not need Canadian-made cars and pressed automakers to shift production south of the border. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has maintained that any agreement with the United States must leave Canada with a viable auto sector.

Ottawa has been pushing for a deal that will put the effective tariff rate for Canadian vehicle exports to the United States on an even keel with those built south of the border but has been hard-pressed to get there, [Automotive Parts Manufacturers' Association president, Flavio] Volpe mentioned.

According to recent reports, as negotiators closed in on a deal this summer by pitching a broader parts exemption, the U.S. offer would have left Canadian autos facing up an effective tariff of up to 7.5 per cent tariffs, he said. While an improvement over the roughly 12.5 per cent rate automakers face today, it is still higher than the industry's profit margin, making it too high for Ottawa to accept, Volpe added.

Canadian negotiators are "not religious" about what mechanism is used to bring the effective tariff rate down, Volpe said, but want to put plants on both sides of the border back on an even playing field.

Counterintuitively, U.S. assembly plants are not immune to tariffs.

Parts compliant with the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement reach U.S. assembly lines tariff-free, but American-made vehicles compliant with the trade deal can include 25 per cent parts content from overseas. That content faces up to 25-per-cent tariffs, translating into a tariff rate on U.S.-made vehicles of as much as 6.5 per cent.

A 3.75-per-cent MSRP credit for American-made vehicles offered by the U.S. Department of Commerce — effective through 2030 — offsets part of these added costs.

But even automakers building USMCA-compliant vehicles in the United States can face an effective tariff rate of 2.75 per cent. The tally can be more or less, depending on where companies source their parts.

The five automakers that currently produce vehicles in Canada — the Substantial Three, Honda and Toyota — are pushing hard for an interim deal that would close or eliminate the tariff gap between Canadian and U.S. plants, even if it's a short-term solution.

In a recent development, right now, there's no real timetable for when a deal could be reached, though Canadian pundits are actually aware that Trump has threatened to hike tariffs to 50% at the start of 2027. While they don't think it'll happen, with Trump, it can never be truly ruled out.

It has been revealed that A former Volkswagen engineer pleaded guilty to insider trading based on secret information he possessed about the automaker's planned $5 billion joint venture with electric vehicle maker Rivian. Michael Stamp pleaded guilty to securities fraud in a Manhattan federal court as part of a deal with prosecutors, confessing that he used his brokerage accounts to buy Rivian shares and options while in possession of confidential information about the merger that he had learned from another employee.

As we previously reported, the 31-year-old and another former VW engineer, Marcus Plank, were charged in July with making a combined $300,000 trading before the Rivian deal was unveiled publicly. Prosecutors mentioned Stamp made a cool quarter million, and Plank made $50,000 while also passing information to a family member who made $12,000. From Bloomberg:.

"I knew that what I was doing was wrong and a breach of my duty to my employer," Stamp remarked at a hearing before a federal judge.

Volkswagen and Rivian declared the deal on June 26, 2024, giving Rivian a financial lifeline as manufacturers large and small began to rethink strategies in a slowing market for electric vehicles.

It has been revealed that stamp and Plank, who were both living in San Jose, California, while on assignment from Germany, were initially charged with conspiracy and securities fraud and faced as much as 25 years in prison if convicted of the most serious counts at trial. Plank has pleaded not guilty and is free on a $500,000 bond.

Recent findings suggest that prosecutors noted internet searches made around the time of the crimes indicated that the two men knew what they were doing was illegal. Just eight days before the announcement, Stamp — that goofus — searched for "statute of limitations insider trading," according to the government. Soon after, Plank's aforementioned family member searched in German "how is insider trading prosecuted?".

Well, significant dog, this is how it's prosecuted — unless you're very rich or in Congress.

There's another fun chapter in the war over Stellantis' Brampton Assembly plant in Ontario, Canada. Now, it's spilled over into court as the automaker has filed a lawsuit against the Unifor workers' union, alleging it is impeding an environmental assessment necessary for the sale to defense contractor Roshel to go through.

In documents filed in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice, Stellantis noted it is seeking an injunction that would require the union, its national president Lana Payne and Unifor Local 1285 plant chairperson Ardis Snow to stop blocking the Brampton plant and preventing work at the site. The manufacturer wants the court to declare that the union has trespassed at the facility and "obstructed the lawful entrance to and exit from the premises." From Automotive News:.

A statement of claim stated union officials are "physically preventing, impeding, and restricting Stellantis' ability to provide access to the premises" to environmental consulting firm Pinchin Ltd.

According to recent reports, pinchin was retained by Roshel — the armoured vehicle manufacturer that agreed to buy the idled Brampton plant from Stellantis for an undisclosed amount earlier this month — to carry out environmental work starting Nov. 9, according to the documents.

However, Stellantis said that morning, union representatives blockaded entrances to the plant with trucks, pylons and individuals carrying Unifor flags and that Unifor told the automaker it wouldn't let Pinchin personnel or equipment through.

"To date, Unifor has continued to obstruct access by persons associated with the environmental work, and Pinchin has not been permitted to perform the environmental work," the statement of claim mentioned.

"Despite Stellantis' reasonable efforts to obtain police assistance, those efforts have not brought the obstruction of or interference with lawful access to the premises under an acceptable degree of control, nor has Pinchin been permitted to access the premises.".

The allegations have not been tested in court.

The statement of claim said Stellantis "is suffering and will continue to suffer irreparable harm and other losses," although the extent of those losses "are extremely difficult, if not impossible, to quantify in monetary terms.".

It added that "continued obstruction" of the environmental assessment "threatens to delay or prevent completion of a material diligence step, interfere with the timetable for the proposed transaction, and affect the responsibilities of Stellantis and Roshel following closing of the proposed transaction.".

Stellantis' deal with Roshel is expected to close in mid-December, subject to certain conditions, according to the documents.

In response, Unifor said it has been "demonstrating in support of Canadian jobs at the Brampton plant throughout the past year." Payne said that the sale of the plant to Roshel is "unacceptable" to the union, and it will continue to work with all parties to get a different outcome.

In a recent development, amazon Autos isn't satisfied with taking on just the U.S. automotive industry, so it has turned its attention to the United Kingdom. Early next year, customers in the UK will be able to buy a fresh car right on Amazon.com. It'll be the first time the U.S.-based e-commerce giant expands its auto services to an overseas market. As it was in the U.S., the first brand to team up with Amazon Autos in this endeavor is Hyundai. From The Wall Street Journal:.

With the Amazon Autos platform, customers will be able to browse real-time dealer inventory, see upfront pricing, get an instant trade-in valuation, connect with a local dealer, as well as reserve a car, the statement said.

According to recent reports, hyundai's IONIQ series as well as its i20 and KONA models will be available on the platform. More brands and dealer partners will be unveiled before its launch.

Around $1.3 trillion of cars were sold by dealerships in the U.S. last year, according to the National Automobile Dealers Association.

Amazon Autos was first rolled out in December of 2024, and the program has expanded to over 150 cities in that time, and it now sells vehicles from 35 brands. I'd expect a similar sort of expansion in the U.S. in due time.

The neat trick with Amazon Autos is that you can sort of use it how you want to. Some customers use the platform from start to finish, visiting the dealership just to pick up the vehicle. However, some start the process on Amazon and then visit the dealership to apply for financing or finish the process. Amazon may be, uh, bad, but I do appreciate that sort of choice and flexibility.

WTI Crude Oil futures and Brent Crude prices are little changed, though, sitting at  $83 and $90, respectively, at the time of publication.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that well, far beyond suspicions, reporting implies that this is really going to happen, and may even be on the verge of happening.
  • Recent findings suggest that “Musk mentioned on SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call last month ​that a merger unifying his AI, robotics, EV and aerospace ambitions ​under a single corporate roof would be ‘a good idea,'” Reuters also noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s been the expectation for months, since SpaceX’s IPO at least, that Tesla and SpaceX will merge. The suspicions haven’t been built on a lot of evidence, more so just the sense that this is what Elon Musk would like to do — including because it would give him basically unchecked control of the combined manufacturer (more so than he already has).

Recent findings suggest that well, far beyond suspicions, reporting implies that this is really going to happen, and may even be on the verge of happening. The Financial Times reports that Tesla and SpaceX have appointed a total of five directors from their boards to explore the possibility — three directors from Tesla’s board and two from SpaceX’s board. In fact, we even know the people who have been appointed — Robyn Denholm (Tesla), Kathleen Wilson-Thompson (Tesla), Jack Hartung (Tesla), Roelof Botha (SpaceX), and Randy Glein (SpaceX).

Recent findings suggest that “Musk mentioned on SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call last month ​that a merger unifying his AI, robotics, EV and aerospace ambitions ​under a single corporate roof would be ‘a good idea,'” Reuters also noted. “He confirmed that the companies had formed special committees of independent directors to discuss ​a union.”.

When this idea first came up, the big glitch that was raised is that Tesla is heavily dependent on China — for both sales and production — and SpaceX is a key military supplier. China could, therefore, put strong pressure on the manufacturer to make it do what China wants. SpaceX would, in essence, be compromised. Whether or not there’s a way around that or it matters in this era of Trump’s massive corruption, I don’t know. Just look at what has happened and is happening with NVIDIA — the CEO (Jensen Huang) was having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, NVIDIA then went ahead and did what China wanted it to do (with the support of President Trump, whom NVIDIA’s CEO heavily supported), Huang was forced out of NVIDIA after it was revealed he had been having an affair with this spy (as well as other people, including employees), and now he’s been welcomed back to NVIDIA after Trump remarked a few things and the board had a long, heart-to-heart talk with Huang. With that story in mind, not to mention the insane levels of corruption Trump and his family have been engaging in, is the Trump administration going to have any issue with the national security concerns that would be raised from Tesla and SpaceX merging?

We’ll see what happens, but at the moment, it sure looks like a merger is on the horizon.

Tech Report: These Are The Non-Car Vehicles You've Crashed

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1559 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, crashing a car is a nightmare of physics, emotion and bodily injury.
  • Unsurprisingly, the Honda ATC makes multiple appearances in the comments section.
  • Man, they really don't make them like these vehicles anymore, and thank god.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, crashing a car is a nightmare of physics, emotion and bodily injury. The seriousness of the forces involved rarely make for a funny story. Luckily, these stories are not that. Earlier this week we asked you what vehicles you've crashed that were not cars, and it's clear some of you had childhoods built on survivor bias. Well, I, for one, am glad you survived ditching mountain bikes off of mountains and crashing lawnmowers into houses. Not just because you're still alive but, most importantly, you're alive and contributing to Jalopnik. That's right, you're still here for a very good reason.

Unsurprisingly, the Honda ATC makes multiple appearances in the comments section. Those three-wheeled off-roading vehicles are up their with lawn darts in the damage they caused Gen Xers. They were eventually banned in the U.S. because of the carnage. But you don't need to buy a dangerous vehicle to make it dangerous. Other interesting entries: a gas grill, a horse and a homemade go-kart.

Man, they really don't make them like these vehicles anymore, and thank god.

Just remembered the weirdest thing I've crashed.

Sources indicate that my dad had some land in West Virginia. There was a tiny river there and it had some very mild rapids that were more of a ford than a rapids, because it was no more than a foot deep. My sister and I would inflate air mattresses and ride them down the "rapids" normally joined by a dog riding a surfboard that was just a piece of foam shaped like one. Most of the time, the dog made the rapids fine, while my sister and I would run into rocks and the like with the air mattresses. Normally after a week of running the rapids, the air mattresses would be completely ruined by running into branches and sharp rocks.

Growing up, dad got a riding lawnmower (Sears 10 hp). Dad morphed it into also being a snow plow with weights on the rear wheels, a homemade plow and a lever to lift and lower it. We had it for years and we took absolutely no care of it other than making sure it had oil before we cranked it up.

One day, it went missing. By this time, it was at peak jank, with a pull starter, blades that never stopped and an uneven deck that was set to dang near chopping up the roots of the grass. It didn't take Columbo to figure how where it was, as we traced a scalped path through many neighbors' lawns and to the river about 1/2 mile away, where the path of 5 O-clock shadow grass ended and the river began. Some drunk teenager discovered that the brake pedal was disconnected, but didn't discover the way to stop it was to drop it into low gear and turn off the engine.

It has been revealed that oh jeez, that's a list. Dirt bikes of all sizes, same with quads a trike or two, several flavours of boat including a canoe (that shoal jumped in front of me!) but probably the most memorable, or at least the most story worthy is the scooter my buddies dad rented for us when we went on a joint family vacation to Cancun back in the late 90s.

Sources indicate that he rented four, two for me and my friend, one for him and one for the older brother and we went ripping around Playa Langosta the way three teens and an adult that branded himself the 'fun' dad could. Getting progressively dumber and riskier as the afternoon wore on. Eventually as the rental time was running out we decided to make a race of it and I was confident enough after a few hours of pinning that little 50cc Honda that I figured I could lean it like a race bike around a corner.

I could not and luckily came away with it with minimal road rash and a big ol bruise on my shoulder.

Recent findings suggest that the scooter was not so lucky, nor was the magazine stand it slid into. Fortunately insurance had been purchased, unfortunately fun dad was not so fun the remaining days of the trip.

In a recent development, I've had my share of mountain bike crashes. The most recent bad one was on a slightly downhill rock field (a bunch of bowling ball sized boulders packed into the trail for 60 feet as a technical feature).

I was going a little too fast, got off the proper line, and went down on my side. Normally this wouldn't be a big deal except rock fields are not very forgiving.

I cracked a couple of ribs which was problematic in that this trail didn't have any short cuts out so I had to ride another 8 miles or so in not very good condition as it was very painful to breathe.

Industry observers note that I was sore for a couple months. I also learned to no longer judge NFL QBs who wear flack jackets to protect their ribs. Most painful injury I've ever had. You just have to gut it out.

According to recent reports, back in the '80's my uncle had a farm that I would go work/play on in the summer. My uncle and cousins had just gotten four ATC200 three wheelers that Spring and my cousins and I were all super excited to race 'em all over the farm that summer. I get up there right after school ends and immediately we're off riding through ditches, bombing across fields and having a blast. The big red barn on the farm was at the top of a steep hill with a gravel drive up to and around it. We'd practice to screaming up the gravel drive and as it leveled out, use the negative G-force to whip the tail out into a lurid slide/drift all the way around the barn. On the other side of the barn was the Milking House, so you'd carry the slide between the two buildings with the echo of the screaming 4 stroke bouncing off the walls. Gaining confidence in this technique, we would just continually elevate the speed. First getting air at the top of the hill, then starting the slide later and eventually clipping apexes and throwing gravel everywhere. This abruptly came to an end when I came up the hill the fastest I'd ever gone, got a late start in my slide, went way too wide and clipped the front corner of the milking house on the other side of the barn. The rear axle of the ATC snapped, throwing me over the bars into the side of the milking house and onto the gravel in a heap. This led to the saying in our family, "that boy couldn't hit the broad side of a barn, but sure can nail a milking house!".

Recent findings suggest that I crashed a Honda ATC when I was maybe 11 or 12 years old. Going way too fast in a large horse pasture when I hit a large dip. Flipped me over, and I'm lucky it didn't land on me. Walked away with a black eye and some scrapes and bruises. 0/10 – do not recommend.

Gen X survivor checking in: if you haven't flipped or nearly paralyzed yourself with a Honda 3-wheeler ATC, you're not really one of us.

From Black Mac and cdoggyd and BuddyS and others (so many others).

My dad built me a homemade go-kart with a 5-hp Briggs & Stratton engine. This was no professional shifter kart chassis. It's exactly what you envision when you think "homemade." Only the right rear wheel was powered. We would take it to the local elementary school on weekends because it had a really large asphalt playground out back and no gates. I'd rip laps for a while until I got tired and we'd go home.

Recent findings suggest that I always went clockwise around the lot. Then one day, I decided I wanted to turn left like my heroes in NASCAR. I got a nice lesson in centrifugal force with the powered wheel now on the inside. It pushed me wide and I hit the curb that separated the asphalt lot with the grass field. I did my best Tony Hawk impression as I did a curb grind for several feet on the floor of the cart. What really stood out to me later is that luckily it happened where it did and not the other side of the lot which would have submarined me under a metal bench face first.

Sources indicate that there isn't anything that moves I probably haven't crashed. Motorcycles, boats, 4 wheelers, snowmobiles, sleds, coaster wagons, bicycles, wheelbarrows, gas grill, and more. Even hit the house with a lawn mower. I learned a zero steer mower sometimes has "zero" steer on wet grass.

Raleigh Chopper. Tore-off a toenail (riding true 1969 style – barefoot in bellbottoms) and broke a tooth. Good times!

Golf carts are my greatest fear in the world because I watched too many camp counselors drive them like demo derby cars. More than once I saw someone try to do a J-turn on one and roll it over and I was certain I just watched someone die.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
Florida court tosses Tampa General Hospital's suit against Eli Lilly over 340B discounts" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

A Florida federal court has tossed Tampa General Hospital's lawsuit against Eli Lilly over the 340B drug discount program.

It has been revealed that florida's Middle District court dismissed the case on a motion from the drugmaker on Wednesday. If Tampa General Hospital wants to file an amended complaint, it must do so within 30 days.

The hospital initially sued the pharmaceutical company over a policy it implemented that requires providers to submit claims-level data on pharmacy and medical dispensing if they participate in 340B. Lilly said it would pull back discounts for providers that did not comply with the requirement and has done so for several organizations, drawing ire from the industry.

Tampa General stated the decision is "unconscionable and immoral" in the initial complaint, filed in July.

According to recent reports, however, the district court argued that Supreme Court precedent holds that organizations like hospitals do not have the private right to sue if they have been charged beyond the threshold, based on a 2011 decision. SCOTUS noted that the right to sue was not outlined by Congress, so it is not an avenue available to these organizations.

"The Court made clear that there is simply no private remedy to superintend the pricing and provision of these discounted drugs," per the order.

"To permit this suit would be to encourage piecemeal litigation and defeat the [Supreme] Court’s insistence on maintaining the Congressional blueprint 'harmoniously and on a uniform, nationwide basis,'" according to the document.

Eli Lilly cheered the decision in a statement.

Sources indicate that "Today’s decision is an key step toward a more transparent 340B program," a Lilly spokesperson mentioned. "Lilly’s claims data requirement asks hospitals for basic information—information they already give insurers every day—to prevent unlawful duplicate discounts.".

According to recent reports, "Decades of HRSA guidance and two federal appeals courts confirm that Lilly can lawfully require this information," the drugmaker said. "More than 3,200 hospitals and clinics already share it with Lilly, and we hope Tampa General Hospital will join them.".

Tampa General Hospital has sued Eli Lilly and Manufacturer over the drugmaker’s “unconscionable and immoral” rescindment of discounted pricing under the 340B program.

It has been revealed that the complaint, filed last week for the U.S. District Court in the Middle District of Florida, is early legal fallout from a policy Lilly implemented earlier this year that requires providers participating in the federal subsidy program to submit claims-level data for all pharmacy and medical dispensations. The company threatened to pull the discounts for those that didn’t comply and made good on its threat for a subset of hospitals last month, sparking outrage among provider groups.

Tampa General, a nearly 1,000-bed disproportionate share hospital, confirmed in the legal complaint that it was among those cut off. It is now spending 25% to 50% more on average for Lilly products, “many of which it must purchase because of Lilly’s status as the market’s only supplier of a given drug product.”.

Sources indicate that tampa General’s lawsuit frequently describes Lilly in such terms, framing the drugmaker as holding significant monopoly power and wielding it in violation of the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act. It also often draws contrast to the 340B program’s intent to support the margins of safety-net hospitals providing care to vulnerable patients, against Lilly’s current status as the largest pharmaceutical firm in the world by market cap.

A spokesperson for Lilly, in a statement given to Fierce Healthcare, described the lawsuit as “just another part of the broader hospital campaign to fight transparency and hide the fraud, waste and abuse that plague the 340B program.”.

Tampa General asked the court to order an immediate end to Lilly’s policy and to award damages for the higher prices to which the hospital was subjected. It contends Lilly’s alleged failure to comply with 340B pricing requirements and decision to continue marketing its products as 340B-discounted are unfair trade practices under the Florida statute.

“The most valuable pharmaceutical tech giant in the world is engaged in a campaign to transfer dollars earmarked for charitable purposes into its own pocket,” the complaint reads. “The direct and inevitable result of Lilly’s actions is reduced healthcare for poor people. Its actions shock the conscience and are self-evidently unconscionable.”.

Tampa General, similar to the hospital associations that have protested Lilly’s policy, contends that the claims data it requires imposes substantial administrative burden on 340B providers. Even “hospitals who have caved to Lilly’s newly introduced demands” have effectively had the prices for their covered outpatient drugs increased due to those administrative costs, it wrote in the complaint.

Industry observers note that lilly and other drugmakers who have signaled similar plans have said they need claims data to spot instances in which a drug purchase is improperly granted multiple discounts under overlapping programs. The firm has also disputed that the burden of its policy is as substantial as hospitals say.

Sources indicate that “The claims data Lilly requires hospitals to share is information they already collect and send to insurers regularly,” the Lilly spokesperson mentioned of the lawsuit’s claims. “Refusing to share that same data with Lilly demonstrates that hospitals are more concerned with hiding rampant abuse in the program than improving its integrity. Lilly will keep working to ensure this program serves vulnerable patients instead of hospitals and their for-profit partners.”.

The 340B program has proven to be a magnet for industry and policy conflict, particularly in recent years as its scale has ballooned. The divide is most evident in the ongoing clash over a pilot rebate program that the Trump administration attempted to launch at the top of the year but was forced to restart after the hospital industry’s legal pushback.

340B providers also received a shock this past week when the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services floated a significant reduction in its 340B reimbursement to 33.4% below average sales price in its annual proposed rule on hospital outpatient payments.

Ann Michael Maye has given the Christmas tree she shares with her husband, New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye, a team dress code this year—and even the presents are in red and blue.

Ahead of Thanksgiving, Ann Michael teamed up with Minted to reveal a holiday display that draws as much from her kitchen and her mahjong nights with fellow Patriots wives and girlfriends as it does from the football field.

Photos from the collaboration offer a peek at the finished tree, the couple’s Christmas card, and a fireside game setup with a seat saved for the hostess.

According to recent reports, the tree occupies a sunny corner framed on two sides by tall, white-trimmed windows. It rises nearly to the crown molding, where a scarlet bow sends two wide ribbon tails cascading over the upper branches.

Sources indicate that A blue-and-white patterned armchair sits off to one side. On the other, the gifts have claimed the floor all the way to the window.

In a recent development, in one photo, Ann Michael reaches up to hang a clear ornament bearing a white No. 10, the same number Drake wears on the field. She’s dressed for the occasion in a striped sweater that picks up the reds and blues of the tree, a long brown skirt, and pointed black heels.

A closer view reveals at least two more numbered ornaments, including a 14 and a 74.

Industry observers note that some of the most personal decorations are easy to miss in a wide shot. Small rectangular frames hang vertically from pale ribbons, their blue-and-white borders standing out among the round ornaments.

Sources indicate that each holds a photograph from the past year. In one, two women pose with their arms around each other. Farther up the tree, another group photo is nestled just beneath a gold ornament.

It has been revealed that ann Michael also found room for a miniature version of her “Bakemas” kitchen. Glass cream puffs with ridges of golden pastry and white filling hang alongside embroidered gingerbread figures and a felt stand mixer.

In one close-up, a tiny cupcake with colorful sprinkles peeks out from a branch just below one of the photo frames.

According to recent reports, even the wrapping rewards a closer look. The boxes beneath the tree are covered in deep blue Minted paper with a small repeating pattern.

Some are tied with wide red bows that echo the tree topper, while others have navy or silvery blue ribbons. Personalized tags hang from the packages, several of which are stacked two high beneath the lowest branches.

The couple saved a different color combination for their Christmas card. In another photo, Ann Michael holds up a red-and-green plaid design featuring an outdoor portrait of her and Drake.

A white border leaves just enough space beneath the picture for a simple “Merry Christmas.”.

One ornament choice hints at what Ann Michael has planned beyond decorating.

According to Minted, she plays mahjong with other Patriots players’ partners and included personalized mahjong ornaments on the tree.

By the staircase, a sign gives the game its own holiday billing, welcoming guests to “Merry Mahjong,” hosted by Ann Michael Maye.

For that occasion, Ann Michael traded her striped sweater for a sleeveless red dress with a floral scarf tied at the waist.

Industry observers note that she poses beside a dark wood banister draped with evergreen garland. A long spray of greenery falls nearly to the floor at the foot of the stairs, secured with burgundy ribbon that picks up the color of her dress.

The game tables are set beside a lit brick fireplace, where patterned stockings hang from a white mantel topped with greenery and tall red candles.

At the nearest table, wooden tile racks frame a blue-and-white playing mat with a large flower at its center.

A second game is ready to go by the window, and a red drink garnished with a sprig of greenery sits within reach of the first.

Ann Michael carried the personalization right down to the seating. Ribbons fasten little name tags to the backs of the bamboo-style chairs, each fitted with a blue-and-white striped cushion.

In the final fireside portrait, she takes her place at the tiles. The tag tied behind her reads “Ann Michael.”.

In a recent development, drake and Ann Michael, both 23, tied the knot in June 2025, having met in middle school in North Carolina. The couple purchased their first home together in Massachusetts in April—and moved in together in July, after Ann Michael graduated from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, where they both attended college.

Since graduating, Ann Michael has been by her husband's side for almost all of his games, traveling across the U.S. to many of the Patriots' matchups—while also continuing to share insights into her experiences online, earning a legion of followers in the process.

To date, Ann Michael boasts more than 1 million followers across TikTok and Instagram, where she reveals what life is really like as one of the NFL's most popular WAGs—a term that refers to the wives and girlfriends of high-profile athletes.

Ann Michael first rose to social media stardom for her baking skills, which she has heavily documented online.

Drake has admitted that he is not blessed with the same skills as his wife in the kitchen and leaves the baking to her, confessing that the most he can whip up is a "good bacon, egg, and cheese.".

During a press conference, Drake gushed about his wife, noting that he was grateful for her support during his career.

“After we got married, she came up here and had never lived up North. [She] had never seen this much snow on the ground, so obviously it was an adjustment for her," he said.

Recent findings suggest that "She’s loved it, she’s loved the people up here, living up here, [and] she loves the support. She’s got her own little journey that’s been awesome, being herself, and that’s the best thing about her and what I love her for.".

Recent findings suggest that he added, “Her watching my middle school football games playing quarterback to now getting a chance to watch me in the Super Bowl ... I wouldn’t rather do it with anybody else.".

The football star also commented on his decision to marry early, after the couple tied the knot in 2025.

Sources indicate that “My teammates have the right to whatever they choose, but I would definitely advise them to eventually get married. It’s one of the best things I’ve experienced in my life. There’s no better feeling than coming home to a wife that loves you and cares for you.

In a recent development, “I know my teammates, some of them are experiencing different parts of their life. I chose to get married young, and I don’t regret it one bit,” he said.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the Intertubes are practically bursting at the seam with news of another step towards the merger of Tesla and SpaceX, both of which are helmed by on-again, off-again Trump supporter Elon Musk.
  • Industry observers note that before you get too excited, Ford is not exactly taking over the space business, nor is it necessarily competing against SpaceX.
  • Alongside its newly minted minority ownership status, the automaker will apply its manufacturing experience to help kickstart Revolution’s spacecraft platform into volume production.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Intertubes are practically bursting at the seam with news of another step towards the merger of Tesla and SpaceX, both of which are helmed by on-again, off-again Trump supporter Elon Musk. Buried beneath the avalanche of press is another automotive-aerospace mashup, that being Ford Motor Company’s newly unveiled investment in the US startup Revolution Space. Evidently the iconic automaker is particularly interested in Revolution’s “unique in-space propulsion technologies.” Hmmm…interesting!

Industry observers note that before you get too excited, Ford is not exactly taking over the space business, nor is it necessarily competing against SpaceX. Revolution specializes in spacecraft, not rocket rolls out. In addition, Ford is not merging itself with Revolution. On November 23, Ford revealed that it is taking up a minority stake in the startup for a yet-to-be-disclosed sum, through its Industrial Platform LLC subsidiary.

Alongside its newly minted minority ownership status, the automaker will apply its manufacturing experience to help kickstart Revolution’s spacecraft platform into volume production.

So, what does Ford have that Revolution wants? Apparently, lots. “With Ford’s manufacturing capabilities, the companies are partnering to industrialize Revolution Space’s next-generation spacecraft at scale, unlocking upcoming dynamic missions and proliferated constellations,” Ford explained in a press statement.

Ford’s Chief Strategy Officer, Marin Gjaja, also chipped in his two cents, emphasizing that “Ford’s strength is building complex products in large volumes, something today’s growing satellite market requires.”.

Industry observers note that gjaja also underscored Ford’s immediate interest in the matter, which is to diversify and harden itself against the shifting winds of the global auto market — presumably including the abrupt shift in federal energy policy here in the US, too. As cited by Ford, the “space economy” currently registers about $600 billion globally, which is peanuts compared to the $1.8 trillion anticipated by 2035.

“Increasingly scaled satellite manufacturing is one of the drivers of that growth,” Ford further explains, noting that the firm Future Market Insights estimates the global satellite manufacturing market in the range of $87–$114 billion by 2035, heads and shoulders above the current estimate of $22–$26 billion.

If all goes according to plan, Revolution Space will give the automaker a hand in government and commercial satellite applications. Ford lists communications, Earth observation, navigation, space domain awareness, satellite servicing, and scientific and deep-space missions among the areas of interest. One can  safely assume that military applications are in there somewhere, too.

Industry observers note that as for what Ford may expect in return in terms of technology transfer, that remains to be seen. Ford notes that its experience in the aerospace field includes building communications and weather satellites for NASA and the military here in the US, as well as NATO.

However, that work goes back 50-60 years ago. The satellites of today are a different creature. “Revolution Space delivers and operates advanced space systems with superior performance and propulsion technologies designed to achieve the precision control and sustained maneuverability to enhance existing and create latest, high-value, dynamic missions,” Ford notes.

In the November 24 announcement, Ford also notes that it has deployed its manufacturing experience to pivot into upcoming fields as called for, citing the bombers it built during World War II and, more recently, the ventilators and protective equipment it supplied during the outset of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Drones could be next on the menu. Coincidentally or not, on November 24, the Wall Street Journal reported that Ford is in the running to help supply drones to the Department of Defense, alongside General Motors among other stakeholders. If realized, the program would call for supplying actuators, engines, sensors, lidar and other elements to drone manufacturers.

“Defense Department leaders have spent months enlisting automakers and their well-established supply chains to help scale up production of everything from missiles to tactical trucks. Now, they want those companies to help ease shortages of unmanned systems, including surveillance and strike drones, that have become crucial in global conflicts,” WSJ elaborated.

Good luck with that. Don’t expect anything of consequence to materialize until Defense Secretary Pete Hesgeth leaves office, either voluntarily or by virtue of impeachment over the hash he has made of the Defense Department, including its equipment as well as its personnel.

Still, the WSJ report did yield an interesting nugget about Ford’s minority stake in Revolution Space. For those without a subscription, the Detroit Free Press kindly offers a summary citing Ford spokesperson David Tovar, who noted that Ford has “had discussions with the Pentagon” focusing on its recent investment in Revolution Space, as well as the manufacture of vehicles for the military.

Recent findings suggest that that’s a good question. The Revolution website is rather thin on the technology itself, though it does note that the board is chaired by former NASA administrator Daniel Goldin, with former NASA astronaut Paul W. Richards serving as Chief Engineer and Chief Strategy Officer.

According to recent reports, revolution does drop a few hints about its expectations for the manufacturing hookup with Ford. The company notes that in 2025 it was selected for the DARPA “LASSO” program, with DARPA being short for the Defense Advanced Research Agency.

DARPA describes LASSO as a program aimed at “significantly increasing the United States’ ability to conduct operations in support of space situational awareness by developing both autonomous satellite navigation in stressing orbital conditions and increasing satellite maneuverability through continuous dynamic repositioning based on changing conditions, with the added benefit of creating a proven reserve model for resources relevant to ISRU on Earth’s Moon,” with ISRU being short for in-situ resource utilization.

It has been revealed that if you guessed water on the moon is the aim, run right out and buy yourself a cigar. “The program seeks performers to design, test, build, and deliver a spacecraft capable of determining all areas on the Moon that contain greater than 5% water concentration,” DARPA explains.

The LASSO selection comes on the heels of a flurry of activity in 2024, when Revolution reported that it was awarded a slot in the “Advanced Capabilities & Demonstration Missions” program of the Defense Innovation Unit. DIU also deployed its fast-track authority under the “Other Transactions” program to tap Revolution for an award in support of the company’s responsive modular electrospray thrust technology.

In 2024 Revolution Space also reported that it earned an award from the Defense Department’s “Accelerate the Procurement and Fielding of Innovative Technologies” program, and it nailed down an agreement with NASA to collaborate on space technology.

As for the Tesla-SpaceX merger, if you have any thoughts about that drop a note in the comment thread.
